pages.body:
Why This Book Exists


Have you ever looked at a blueprint? It is a plan. It is a drawing. It shows you what a building will look like before it is built. It shows you the walls. It shows you the doors. It shows you the windows. A blueprint is a promise. It is a promise that something is coming.


The book of Genesis is a blueprint. It is the first book of the Bible. It is the book of beginnings. It tells us how the world began. It tells us how humanity began. It tells us how sin began. But it also tells us how the rescue began. It is a blueprint. It is a plan. It is a promise. And hidden in its pages is the gospel. Hidden in its stories is Jesus.


This book is for the curious. It is for the spiritual seeker who senses there is more. It is for the person who wants to understand the ancient text. Over the next 30 days, we are going to look at 30 stories from Genesis. We are going to decode them. We are going to see what they were really pointing to. And we are going to discover that the first book of the Bible is not just a history book. It is a gospel book. It is the first blueprint. And the blueprint is Jesus.


The Value You Will Get


By the end of this book, you will not see Genesis as a collection of old stories. You will see it as a divine plan. You will see it as a preparation. You will see it as a prophecy. You will understand the hidden gospel. You will understand the ancient patterns. You will understand why the first book of the Bible matters today. You will have a new confidence in your faith. You will have a new love for your Bible. And you will have a new appreciation for the one who was planned from the beginning.


How to Use This Guide


This is a 30 day journey. Each day takes about 10 minutes. Read the hook. Read the ancient text...

pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever watched a building go up? It starts with a plan. It starts with a blueprint. Someone designs it. Someone draws it. Someone plans every detail. The Bible starts the same way. It starts with a plan. It starts with a blueprint. It starts with creation. And hidden in the story of creation is a clue. It is a clue about Jesus.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth." - Genesis 1:1 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


This is the first verse in the Bible. It is simple. It is short. But it is profound. God created everything. He created the heavens. He created the earth. He created the light. He created the land. He created the animals. He created humanity. He created it all. And He created it with a plan. He created it with a purpose. He created it with a blueprint.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was with God in the beginning. Through him all things were made; without him nothing was made that has been made." - John 1:1-3


The Gospel of John opens with the same words as Genesis. "In the beginning." But John reveals something new. He reveals the Word. The Word was with God. The Word was God. Through Him all things were made. The Word is Jesus. Jesus was there in the beginning. He was the blueprint. He was the plan. He was the creator.


The Verdict
This is not a coincidence. The first verse of the Bible introduces God as the Creator. The first verse of the Gospel of John introduces Jesus as the Creator. The pattern is exact. The blueprint is precise. The plan is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you ever feel like your life is random? Do you ever feel like there is no plan? Remember the blueprint. God created everything with a plan. He created you with a plan. You are not an accident. You are part of the blueprint.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the blueprint. Thank you for the plan. Thank you that you created everything with a purpose. Thank you that you created me with a purpose. Thank you that Jesus was there in the beginning. Help me to see your plan in my life. Help me to trust your blueprint. Amen.

The Hook
Have you ever been in a dark room? Maybe you were in a basement. Maybe the power went out. You could not see anything. You groped for a light switch. You wanted light. The Bible starts with darkness. It starts with a void. It starts with an empty canvas. And then God speaks. And light appears. And hidden in that light is a clue. It is a clue about Jesus.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"And God said, 'Let there be light,' and there was light." - Genesis 1:3 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The earth was formless and empty. Darkness was over the surface of the deep. The Spirit of God was hovering over the waters. And God said, "Let there be light." And there was light. God spoke. And light came. It was the first command. It was the first creation. It was the first step in the blueprint.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness, but will have the light of life." - John 8:12


Jesus is the light. He is the one who shines in the darkness. He is the one who dispels the void. He is the one who brings life. The light in Genesis is a shadow. It is a clue. It is a blueprint. The reality is Jesus.


The Verdict
The first words of God in the Bible are "Let there be light." Jesus is the light of the world. The pattern is exact. The blueprint is precise. The plan is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you feel like you are in darkness? Do you feel like you are in a void? Do you feel like you are empty? Remember the light. God spoke light into the darkness. He can speak light into your darkness. He can speak life into your void. He can speak Jesus into your emptiness.


The Prayer
Jesus, you are the light of the world. Thank you for shining in the darkness. Thank you for dispelling the void. Thank you for bringing life. Shine your light into my heart today. Shine your light into my darkness. Help me to follow you. Help me to walk in your light. Amen.

The Hook
Have you ever tried to build something without instructions? Maybe a piece of furniture. Maybe a toy. Maybe a model. It is frustrating. It is confusing. You end up with extra pieces. You end up with a mess. The Bible is not a mess. The Bible is not random. The Bible is ordered. The Bible is structured. The Bible is a blueprint. And hidden in the order is a clue. It is a clue about Jesus.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"And God said, 'Let there be a vault between the waters to separate water from water.'" - Genesis 1:6 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


God did not just create. He separated. He separated the light from the darkness. He separated the waters from the waters. He separated the land from the sea. He brought order out of chaos. He brought structure out of the void. He brought a blueprint out of the emptiness.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"For God is not a God of disorder but of peace." - 1 Corinthians 14:33


Jesus is the God of order. He is the God of peace. He brings structure to chaos. He brings calm to the storm. He brings peace to the heart. The order in Genesis is a shadow. It is a clue. It is a blueprint. The reality is Jesus.


The Verdict
God brought order out of chaos. Jesus is the God of order. The pattern is exact. The blueprint is precise. The plan is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you feel like your life is chaotic? Do you feel like your life is a mess? Do you feel like you have extra pieces and no instructions? Remember the God of order. He can bring order to your chaos. He can bring peace to your storm. He can bring structure to your void.


The Prayer
Jesus, you are the God of order. Thank you for bringing order out of chaos. Thank you for bringing peace to my storm. Thank you for bringing structure to my void. Bring order to my life today. Bring peace to my heart. Help me to trust your blueprint. Amen.

The Hook
Have you ever seen a seed? It is small. It is simple. It looks like nothing. But inside that seed is life. Inside that seed is a tree. Inside that seed is a future. The Bible is full of seeds. It is full of life. It is full of growth. And hidden in the seed is a clue. It is a clue about Jesus.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Then God said, 'Let the land produce vegetation: seed-bearing plants and trees on the land that bear fruit with seed in it, according to their various kinds.' And it was so." - Genesis 1:11 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


God spoke. And the land produced vegetation. Seed-bearing plants. Trees. Fruit. Life. God did not just create lifeless things. He created living things. He created things that grow. He created things that reproduce. He created things that bear fruit. He created life.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"I am the vine; you are the branches. If you remain in me and I in you, you will bear much fruit; apart from me you can do nothing." - John 15:5


Jesus is the vine. He is the source of life. He is the source of growth. He is the source of fruit. The seed in Genesis is a shadow. It is a clue. It is a blueprint. The reality is Jesus.


The Verdict
God created life. Jesus is the source of life. The pattern is exact. The blueprint is precise. The plan is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you feel lifeless? Do you feel like you are not growing? Do you feel like you are not bearing fruit? Remember the seed. Remember the vine. Jesus is the source of life. He can bring life to your dry places. He can bring growth to your stagnant places. He can bring fruit to your barren places.


The Prayer
Jesus, you are the vine. Thank you for being the source of life. Thank you for being the source of growth. Thank you for being the source of fruit. Bring life to my dry places. Bring growth to my stagnant places. Bring fruit to my barren places. Help me to remain in you. Amen.

The Hook
Have you ever looked at the sky? Have you seen the sun? Have you seen the moon? Have you seen the stars? They are beautiful. They are mysterious. They are signs. The Bible says they are signs. They are markers. They are reminders. And hidden in the sky is a clue. It is a clue about Jesus.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"And God said, 'Let there be lights in the vault of the sky to separate the day from the night, and let them serve as signs to mark sacred times, and days and years.'" - Genesis 1:14 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


God created the sun. He created the moon. He created the stars. They are not accidents. They are signs. They are markers. They are reminders. They mark the days. They mark the seasons. They mark the years. They point to something. They point to someone.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness, but will have the light of life." - John 8:12


Jesus is the light. He is the greater light. He is the light that never sets. He is the light that never fades. The sun and moon in Genesis are shadows. They are clues. They are blueprints. The reality is Jesus.


The Verdict
God created the lights in the sky. Jesus is the light of the world. The pattern is exact. The blueprint is precise. The plan is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you need a sign? Do you need a marker? Do you need a reminder? Look at the sky. Look at the sun. Look at the moon. Look at the stars. They are signs. They are reminders. They point to the one who made them. They point to Jesus.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the sun. Thank you for the moon. Thank you for the stars. Thank you for the signs in the sky. Thank you for the reminders. Help me to look up. Help me to see the signs. Help me to see Jesus. Amen.

pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever been to the ocean? Have you seen the fish? Have you seen the whales? Have you seen the creatures of the deep? They are beautiful. They are mysterious. They are alive. The Bible says God created them. He created them all. And hidden in the sea is a clue. It is a clue about Jesus.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"So God created the great creatures of the sea and every living thing with which the water teems and that moves about in it, according to their kinds, and every winged bird according to its kind. And God saw that it was good." - Genesis 1:21 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


God created the sea creatures. He created the great creatures. He created the small creatures. He created the fish. He created the birds. He created them all. He saw them. He called them good. He blessed them.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"As Jesus was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon called Peter and his brother Andrew. They were casting a net into the lake, for they were fishermen. 'Come, follow me,' Jesus said, 'and I will send you out to fish for people.'" - Matthew 4:18-19


Jesus called fishermen. He called them to follow Him. He called them to fish for people. The sea creatures in Genesis are a shadow. They are a clue. They are a blueprint. The reality is Jesus.


The Verdict
God created the sea creatures. Jesus called fishermen to fish for people. The pattern is exact. The blueprint is precise. The plan is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you feel like you are drowning? Do you feel like you are lost at sea? Remember the fishermen. Remember the one who calmed the sea. Jesus is the one who saves. He is the one who rescues. He is the one who calls you out of the deep.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for the sea. Thank you for the creatures. Thank you for the fishermen. Thank you for calling me. Help me to follow you. Help me to fish for people. Help me to trust you in the deep waters. Amen.

pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever wondered why you are here? Have you ever wondered what your purpose is? Have you ever wondered who you are? The Bible answers these questions. It answers them in the very first book. It answers them in the very first chapter. It answers them with a blueprint. And hidden in that blueprint is a clue. It is a clue about Jesus.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Then God said, 'Let us make mankind in our image, in our likeness, so that they may rule over the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky, over the livestock and all the wild animals, and over all the creatures that move along the ground.'" - Genesis 1:26 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


God created humanity. He created them in His image. He created them in His likeness. He created them to rule. He created them to have dominion. He created them to be His representatives. He created them with a purpose. He created them with a blueprint.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"The Son is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn over all creation." - Colossians 1:15


Jesus is the image of the invisible God. He is the true image. He is the perfect likeness. The humanity in Genesis is a shadow. It is a clue. It is a blueprint. The reality is Jesus.


The Verdict
God created humanity in His image. Jesus is the image of the invisible God. The pattern is exact. The blueprint is precise. The plan is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you feel like you have no purpose? Do you feel like you have no value? Remember the blueprint. You are created in the image of God. You are created with a purpose. You are created with value. You are not an accident. You are part of the plan.


The Prayer
God, thank you for creating me. Thank you for creating me in your image. Thank you for giving me purpose. Thank you for giving me value. Help me to see myself the way you see me. Help me to live out my purpose. Help me to reflect your image. Amen.
pages.title: Day 8: The Blueprint of Humanity

pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever been tired? Have you ever been exhausted? Have you ever needed a break? We all have. We all need rest. The Bible starts with rest. It starts with a day off. It starts with a blueprint. And hidden in that rest is a clue. It is a clue about Jesus.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"By the seventh day God had finished the work he had been doing; so on the seventh day he rested from all his work. Then God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it he rested from all the work of creating that he had done." - Genesis 2:2-3 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


God created for six days. He worked. He formed. He filled. He made. Then He rested. He stopped. He ceased. He blessed the seventh day. He made it holy. He created a rhythm. He created a blueprint. Work and rest. Labor and cease. Create and enjoy.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest." - Matthew 11:28


Jesus is the rest. He is the true rest. He is the one who gives rest to the weary. The rest in Genesis is a shadow. It is a clue. It is a blueprint. The reality is Jesus.


The Verdict
God rested on the seventh day. Jesus is our rest. The pattern is exact. The blueprint is precise. The plan is Jesus.


The Resonance
Are you tired? Are you weary? Are you burdened? Remember the rest. Remember Jesus. He is the one who gives rest. He is the one who gives peace. He is the one who gives refreshment. You can stop striving. You can stop working. You can rest in Him.


The Prayer
Jesus, I am tired. I am weary. I am burdened. Thank you for being my rest. Thank you for giving me rest. Help me to stop striving. Help me to stop working. Help me to rest in you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 9: The Blueprint of Rest

pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever been to a garden? Have you seen the flowers? Have you seen the trees? Have you seen the fruit? A garden is a place of beauty. It is a place of life. It is a place of peace. The Bible starts with a garden. It starts with a blueprint. And hidden in that garden is a clue. It is a clue about Jesus.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Now the LORD God had planted a garden in the east, in Eden; and there he put the man he had formed. The LORD God made all kinds of trees grow out of the ground—trees that were pleasing to the eye and good for food. In the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil." - Genesis 2:8-9 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


God planted a garden. He planted it in Eden. He put the man there. He made trees grow. Trees that were pleasing to the eye. Trees that were good for food. In the middle of the garden was the tree of life. In the middle of the garden was the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. It was a place of beauty. It was a place of choice. It was a place of blueprints.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Then Jesus said to them, 'Very truly I tell you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life in you. Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise them up at the last day.'" - John 6:53-54


Jesus is the tree of life. He is the one who gives eternal life. The garden in Genesis is a shadow. It is a clue. It is a blueprint. The reality is Jesus.


The Verdict
God planted a garden with the tree of life. Jesus is the tree of life. The pattern is exact. The blueprint is precise. The plan is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you want life? Do you want eternal life? Do you want to eat from the tree of life? Remember the garden. Remember Jesus. He is the tree of life. He gives life. He gives eternal life. He gives himself.


The Prayer
Jesus, you are the tree of life. Thank you for giving me life. Thank you for giving me eternal life. Help me to eat from your tree. Help me to feed on your truth. Help me to feast on your love. Amen.

pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever seen a river? Have you seen the water flow? Have you seen the life it brings? A river is a source of life. It is a source of refreshment. It is a source of blessing. The Bible starts with a river. It starts with a blueprint. And hidden in that river is a clue. It is a clue about Jesus.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"A river watering the garden flowed from Eden; from there it was separated into four headwaters." - Genesis 2:10 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


A river flowed from Eden. It watered the garden. It brought life. It brought refreshment. It brought blessing. It was a source of life. It was a source of joy. It was a source of abundance.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Whoever believes in me, as Scripture has said, rivers of living water will flow from within them. By this he meant the Spirit, whom those who believed in him were later to receive." - John 7:38-39


Jesus is the river of living water. He is the source of life. He is the source of refreshment. He is the source of blessing. The river in Genesis is a shadow. It is a clue. It is a blueprint. The reality is Jesus.


The Verdict
A river flowed from Eden. Jesus is the river of living water. The pattern is exact. The blueprint is precise. The plan is Jesus.


The Resonance
Are you thirsty? Are you dry? Are you empty? Remember the river. Remember Jesus. He is the river of living water. He can quench your thirst. He can refresh your soul. He can fill your emptiness.


The Prayer
Jesus, you are the river of living water. Thank you for quenching my thirst. Thank you for refreshing my soul. Thank you for filling my emptiness. Help me to drink from your river. Help me to flow with your Spirit. Amen.

pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever seen a tree? Have you seen the roots? Have you seen the trunk? Have you seen the branches? A tree is a picture of life. It is a picture of growth. It is a picture of strength. The Bible is full of trees. And hidden in the tree is a clue. It is a clue about Jesus.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"The LORD God made all kinds of trees grow out of the ground—trees that were pleasing to the eye and good for food. In the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil." - Genesis 2:9 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


There were two trees in the garden. The tree of life. The tree of the knowledge of good and evil. One was a tree of life. One was a tree of death. One was a tree of obedience. One was a tree of disobedience. One was a tree of blessing. One was a tree of curse. It was a choice. It was a test. It was a blueprint.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"He himself bore our sins in his body on the cross, so that we might die to sins and live for righteousness; by his wounds you have been healed." - 1 Peter 2:24


Jesus is the tree of life. He is also the tree of the cross. He bore our sins on the tree. He took the curse. He took the death. He took the punishment. The tree in Genesis is a shadow. It is a clue. It is a blueprint. The reality is Jesus.


The Verdict
There was a tree of life and a tree of death. Jesus is the tree of life. He took the tree of death. The pattern is exact. The blueprint is precise. The plan is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you want life? Do you want to eat from the tree of life? Do you want to be healed? Remember the tree. Remember the cross. Remember Jesus. He took the curse. He took the death. He took the punishment. He gives life.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for the tree. Thank you for the cross. Thank you for taking the curse. Thank you for taking the death. Thank you for taking the punishment. Thank you for giving me life. Help me to eat from your tree. Help me to live in your life. Amen.
pages.title: Day 12: The Blueprint of the Tree

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever been given a command? Have you ever been given a rule? Have you ever been given a test? We all have. We all have rules. We all have commands. The Bible starts with a command. It starts with a test. It starts with a blueprint. And hidden in that command is a clue. It is a clue about Jesus.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"And the LORD God commanded the man, 'You are free to eat from any tree in the garden; but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, for when you eat from it you will certainly die.'" - Genesis 2:16-17 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


God gave a command. He gave a rule. He gave a test. He said, "You are free to eat from any tree. But you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. For when you eat from it, you will certainly die." It was a command. It was a boundary. It was a blueprint.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous." - Romans 5:19


Adam disobeyed. He broke the command. He ate the fruit. He brought sin into the world. But Jesus obeyed. He kept the command. He never sinned. He brought righteousness into the world. The command in Genesis is a shadow. It is a clue. It is a blueprint. The reality is Jesus.


The Verdict
Adam disobeyed. Jesus obeyed. The pattern is exact. The blueprint is precise. The plan is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you feel like you are always breaking the rules? Do you feel like you are always failing? Do you feel like you are always disobeying? Remember Jesus. He obeyed for you. He kept the command for you. He brought righteousness for you.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for obeying. Thank you for keeping the command. Thank you for bringing righteousness. Thank you for taking my disobedience. Help me to live in your obedience. Help me to live in your righteousness. Amen.
pages.title: Day 13: The Blueprint of the Command

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever been alone? Have you ever been lonely? Have you ever needed help? We all have. We all need help. We all need someone. The Bible starts with a helper. It starts with a companion. It starts with a blueprint. And hidden in that helper is a clue. It is a clue about Jesus.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"The LORD God said, 'It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper suitable for him.'" - Genesis 2:18 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


God said, "It is not good for the man to be alone." He said, "I will make a helper suitable for him." He created the woman. He created Eve. He created a companion. He created a helper. He created a partner. It was a gift. It was a blueprint.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another advocate to help you and be with you forever—the Spirit of truth." - John 14:16-17


Jesus promised a helper. He promised the Holy Spirit. He promised an advocate. He promised a companion. The helper in Genesis is a shadow. It is a clue. It is a blueprint. The reality is the Holy Spirit.


The Verdict
God created a helper for Adam. Jesus promised a helper for us. The pattern is exact. The blueprint is precise. The plan is the Holy Spirit.


The Resonance
Are you lonely? Are you alone? Do you need help? Remember the helper. Remember the Holy Spirit. He is with you. He is your advocate. He is your companion. You are not alone.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for the helper. Thank you for the Holy Spirit. Thank you for being with me. Thank you for being my advocate. Thank you for being my companion. Help me to know the Spirit. Help me to listen to the Spirit. Help me to walk with the Spirit. Amen.
pages.title: Day 14: The Blueprint of the Helper

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever seen a rib? Have you ever seen a bone? Have you ever seen a body? The Bible tells a strange story. It tells a story about a rib. It tells a story about a bone. It tells a story about a woman. And hidden in that rib is a clue. It is a clue about Jesus.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"But for Adam no suitable helper was found. So the LORD God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep; and while he was sleeping, he took one of the man's ribs and then closed up the place with flesh. Then the LORD God made a woman from the rib he had taken out of the man, and he brought her to the man." - Genesis 2:20-22 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


God caused Adam to fall into a deep sleep. He took a rib. He made a woman. He brought her to the man. It was a strange story. It was a beautiful story. It was a blueprint. It pointed to something greater.

END MATTER


The 30-Day Genesis Challenge
You have journeyed through 30 stories in Genesis. Now what? I challenge you to read the Gospel of John. It is 21 chapters. It is the perfect follow-up to this book. It starts with the same words as Genesis. "In the beginning." It will show you how Jesus is the fulfillment of every story. As you read, look for the clues. Look for the blueprint. Look for Jesus.


A Note on Faith
The stories are evidence. They are evidence of a divine plan. But evidence does not save you. The stories point to a person. The stories point to Jesus. You can understand the stories and still miss the truth. The invitation is for your heart. Jesus said, "Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in." The stories are on the table. The door is open. It is your choice.


About the Author
Christine A. writes for the spiritually curious. He is passionate about showing people the hidden wisdom of the Bible. He lives with his family and enjoys good coffee and long conversations with skeptics. He believes that honest questions deserve honest answers.
